result.title: DoseSteer: Steering diffusion-based dose prediction models towards clinical targets via Dual-Response Guidance
result.summary: AI dose-prediction models generate patient-specific 3D dose distributions from patient anatomy. Yet these predictions can still miss structure-level clinical dose targets. Once deployed, most existing predictors offer no direct mechanism to correct such deviations, deferring target enforcement to downstream plan optimization. We introduce DoseSteer, an inference-time framework that steers frozen diffusion-based dose prediction models towards specified clinical targets without retraining. To meet clinical targets while preserving overall dose prediction quality, we propose Dual-Response Guidance (DRG), a structure-centric algorithm that probes the model's responses to perturbations in each structure's noisy dose and context and jointly solves for per-structure steering strengths. Across five dataset-model configurations spanning three diffusion architectures and three datasets, DRG outperforms 12 training-free baselines under identical reference-derived target proxies, removing at least 97% of the target error, reducing the official dose error by 7.8% on average, and improving dose fidelity outside the steered structures. DoseSteer reconciles learned anatomical dose priors with explicit structure-level targets at test time, establishing a principled, training-free mechanism to refine AI dose predictions prior to plan optimization. Code is available at https://github.com/csp2002/DoseSteer.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DoseSteer：在推理时引导冻结的扩散式剂量预测模型，通过探测模型对各个结构噪声剂量与上下文的扰动响应，联合求解逐结构的引导强度（Dual-Response Guidance），在不重训练的情况下满足结构级临床剂量目标。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是医学剂量预测应用而非视觉推理研究，但其「冻结生成模型＋按结构探测响应并联合求解引导强度」的测试时控制思路，可能为 LVR 中按视觉证据子区域分配引导、筛选与停止提供可核查线索。
